clue.text: Modern culture born to accommodate comedian

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so the word for born holds the comedian

parts.note: née, from French, means born and is used before a maiden name
a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: Present-day culture is shown making room for a stand-up comic.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Age movement is a form of late twentieth-century spiritual culture, so modern culture fits it.

clue.text: Lacking school uniform (and worse!), daughter is kept in by group of teachers

indicators.note: kept in by says the daughter and 'is' sit inside the teachers' union

parts.note: the NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A girl detained by staff for breaking uniform rules, or worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist wears no clothes at all, so is without school uniform and much else besides.

clue.text: Fighting force getting forward into hazard — I wouldn't mind that?

indicators.note: into says the force and forward go inside the bet

parts.note: to hazard is to bet, so a wager
RM stands for the Royal Marines, a British fighting force
on means forward, as in 'move on'

explanation.surface: An army pushes forward into danger, and someone shrugs at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' refers back to the fighting in the clue: someone who wants war would not mind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who stirs up conflict would happily accept the fighting the clue describes.

clue.text: Characters in garden about to meet English bigwig

indicators.note: about signals the characters of garden are moved around

explanation.surface: People in a garden are about to meet an important Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a person of high rank or importance, a big shot.

clue.text: Beat the heartless lads up cruelly

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the letters are treated roughly and so rearranged
heartless means the middle letter of the word 'the' is removed

explanation.surface: Some young men are beaten up savagely and without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the H from THE, leaving TE; 'cruelly' rearranges TE with LADS and UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that pulsated throbbed rhythmically, as a heart does, so it beat.

clue.text: Unsettled? Has change of heart, becoming carefree

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for unsettled is swapped for another

parts.note: land with no settlers is uninhabited

explanation.surface: An anxious person changes their mind and relaxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsettled' looks like worried but means lived in by nobody; its middle A becomes I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free of inhibitions means unrestrained and relaxed, close to carefree.

clue.text: Wife of despot? One is 'without seed'

definitions.meaning: the wife of a sultan, a Muslim ruler
the seedless dried grape used in baking

explanation.surface: A tyrant's spouse who bore him no children.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sultan's wife and a pale seedless raisin.

clue.text: Dull time before formal ceremony

indicators.note: before puts the time letter ahead of the ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a solemn ceremony

explanation.surface: A boring wait before a stiff official ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite means hackneyed and unoriginal, so stale and dull.

clue.text: Constable from old country brought into Ulster city

indicators.note: brought into places the old country inside the city

parts.note: Derry is a city in Northern Ireland
GB is Great Britain

explanation.surface: A policeman from the old country is posted to a Northern Irish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogberry is the bumbling constable in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.

clue.text: Greek academic with stifled expression looking back

indicators.note: stifled means held in, so the academic surrounds the reversed word

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: looking back means the word for expression is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a manner or look, an expression on the face

explanation.surface: A Greek lecturer suppresses a backward glance or look.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorians were one of the main peoples of ancient Greece, so a Dorian is a Greek.

clue.text: Author not in the 'in' team

definitions.meaning: Henry ... wrote the novel Tom Jones
in cricket the side not batting, i.e. not in

explanation.surface: A writer is left out of the fashionable group.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the batting side is 'in'; the other side is out in the field, so it is fielding.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the eighteenth-century novelist; the other is the cricket side out in the field, not batting.

clue.text: Crossword finished? Eight letters missing here and there — I'm at sea!

indicators.text: Eight letters missing here and there
indicators.note: eight letters are dropped at several places in the phrase, leaving the rest in order

explanation.surface: A solver who has finished the puzzle, with eight squares blank, admits being lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, R, O, S from the start, N, I from the middle and E, D from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordfish is a large ocean fish, and so it can fairly say it lives out at sea.

clue.text: When given coaching, a learner is using sixth sense

parts.note: being in tuition means receiving teaching
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student taking lessons relies on gut feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuitional means relying on instinct, knowing without reasoning, which is the so-called sixth sense.

clue.text: Singer giving a sign that something has to go

parts.words: sign that something has to go
parts.note: dele is the proofreader's mark ordering a deletion

explanation.surface: A singer gives a signal that something must be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is the British pop vocalist known for the album 21.

clue.text: One going around with big speakers?

definitions.text: One going around with big speakers?

parts.words: One going around with big speakers?
parts.note: suggests a person with loud friends, but it is the large portable stereo carried round the streets

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps company with grand orators.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large portable radio and cassette player with powerful loudspeakers, carried through the streets.

clue.text: Sort of parasite damaging to red meat

indicators.note: damaging says the words to, red and meat are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of parasite that harms red meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trematode is a parasitic flatworm or fluke, a type of parasite.

clue.text: What's put down in a sequence of letters for Spooner to join

indicators.note: Spooner, the clergyman famed for swapping the starts of words, signals the swap of opening sounds

parts.note: the word what, with 's as a link

parts.words: put down in a sequence of letters
parts.note: a word written letter by letter is spelled

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what is written out letter by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'what spelled' and swap the opening W and SP sounds to get 'spot weld'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot-weld is to join metal sheets by welding at separate small points.

clue.text: He and I will certainly contribute to it

definitions.text: He and I will certainly contribute to it

parts.words: He and I will certainly contribute to it
parts.note: He and I look like two people, but they are the symbols of helium and iodine, two chemical elements

explanation.surface: A pair of people promise to make a donation to some cause.
explanation.definitionFit: The chart of chemical elements includes helium (He) and iodine (I) among its entries.

clue.text: Circle somehow can't go into figure with straight sides

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of can't and go are arranged in some new way

explanation.surface: A circle cannot become a shape with straight edges.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is a polygon with eight straight sides.

clue.text: Emotional cases proving to be burdensome?

definitions.text: Emotional cases proving to be burdensome?

parts.words: Emotional cases proving to be burdensome?
parts.note: suggests troubled people who weigh on others

explanation.surface: People in distress who become a heavy load on those around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is a set of travel cases, and emotional baggage is a burden of feelings from the past.

clue.text: Wild rumour Mirror's leader's quashed

indicators.note: quashed means squashed in, so the letter is pressed inside the rumour

parts.note: a story is a tale or rumour

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the newspaper's name

explanation.surface: A sensational piece of gossip is suppressed by the tabloid's editor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy weather or a stormy meeting is turbulent and wild.

clue.text: In diplomacy Italy must be understood

indicators.note: In says the country's letter goes inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is skill in handling people delicately
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Italy must be grasped as part of diplomatic dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied without being spoken, so it is understood rather than stated.

clue.text: Give immunity to Conservative oldie losing it tragically

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic old king who goes mad

explanation.surface: A senior Tory is let off despite losing his temper badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing it' means going mad, as Lear does in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone is to free them of blame or charges, so to exonerate them.

clue.text: After snide remark in pub see worker in high dudgeon

indicators.note: in places the snide remark inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a dig is a cutting remark
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: After a nasty jibe in the bar, one watches a labourer storm off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in high dudgeon is to be deeply resentful or angry, which matches indignant.

clue.text: Coming out with new regimen — grams reduced

indicators.note: new tells us the word regimen is to be made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: grams cut down to its abbreviation g

explanation.surface: Starting a fresh diet that cuts down the grams.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerging means coming out into view, as from hiding.

clue.text: Delight in one being released by liberator

indicators.note: one being released means the I is let go from the word for liberator

parts.note: a saviour is one who rescues or frees
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prisoner revels in being set free by a rescuer.
explanation.definitionFit: To savour something is to relish or enjoy it fully.

clue.text: Newspaper (not Independent) has phone interception, taking chances

indicators.note: interception has the phone word caught within the shortened newspaper
not means the letter for Independent is taken out of the newspaper

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper published every day
to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: A tabloid other than the Independent is caught hacking phones, a risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' leaves DALY; the surface's phone-hacking scandal is a red herring for the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting daringly means acting boldly, with risks taken.

clue.text: Just bank on yours truly

indicators.note: on here says the word for bank comes after the word for yours truly

parts.note: yours truly is a jocular way of saying me
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: Simply trust me.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely means only, simply, as 'just' does in 'just a child'.
